en: Points of Controversy (Kathāvatthu) Great Fifty-Section (Mahāpaṇṇāsaka) Sixth Chapter (Chaṭṭhavagga)
The Discussion on Whether Bodily Action is Visible.
Is bodily action visible? Yes.
Is form the visible base, the element of form— blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by the eye, impinging upon the eye, and coming within the range of the eye?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is bodily action with visibility?
“Yes,” you say.
“But then, is it not the case that eye-consciousness arises in dependence upon both the eye and bodily action?
You must not say so… [and so on].
“Dependent on the eye and bodily action, visual consciousness arises”?—Yes.
“Dependent on the eye and bodily action, visual consciousness arises”—[is this your position]? Yes.
Is there such a sutta? No, there is not.
[But it says:
“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises.”
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes. If it is so, then:
"Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises."
The Sutta passage is indeed thus, yet, alas, you should not say:
“Dependent on the eye and bodily action, eye-consciousness arises.
It should not be so stated.
“Is bodily action visible?”—
Yes. But does one not see [the body] approaching, receding, looking forward, looking around, contracting, and extending?
“Yes, [he does].
“If he sees one approaching, withdrawing, looking forward, looking around, contracting [a limb], or extending [a limb], then indeed, sir, you must say:
‘Bodily action is visible.’”
The discussion on bodily action being visible is finished.
The sixth chapter.
Its summary verse:
The restraint is unconditioned; dependent origination is unconditioned; the four truths are unconditioned;
the four formless attainments are unconditioned; the attainment of cessation is unconditioned; space is unconditioned; space with visibility;
the four great elements; the five faculties; and likewise bodily action.
